_comment: Which local tests run on GitHub Actions, and in which order they are turned on.  Enabling more is a reviewed edit of this file.
The single workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml compiles once per platform ('build' job), uploads the workspace, then runs every
(platform, lane) pair that has an enabled entry as its own job ('test' jobs, in parallel, each on a fresh machine, so lanes cannot
interfere through ports, config directories or temp files). Test assemblies are prebuilt; some integration journeys restore temporary fixture projects using the populated package cache.
throughBatch: entries whose batch is greater than this are planned but not run.  workflow_dispatch can override it.

focus: true runs only the 'observe' entries on each platform (a 'required' one has passed twice in a row), which saves runner time while many entries still fail; a lane left with no entry is not scheduled.  workflow_dispatch with full=true runs everything once; set focus to false to return to full runs.
Per platform an entry is 'observe' (runs; a failure is reported as a warning and does not fail the job), 'required' (a failure fails
the job) or 'excluded' (does not run; 'reason' says why).  A platform missing from an entry is excluded.  A new batch starts as 'observe';
promote it to 'required' after it has been green on that platform for several runs.
kind: xunit-exe = dotnet <target> [args] (an xUnit v3 test assembly, run directly); msbuild = dotnet msbuild <target> -t:Build.
'project' is built once in the build job (distinct projects only).  'measuredSeconds' is the last measured duration; keep it current when promoting a batch.

'buildFirst' projects are built before everything else on every platform that builds: the host's build writes the host-assembly manifest that lets every add-in trim what the host already ships (without it each add-in carries ~550 MB of copy-local dependencies and AddIns reaches 13 GB); tests/OpenDevelop.IntegrationTests/TESTING.md says the same: build the application first.

'buildArgs' are extra dotnet build arguments for the entry's 'project'; entries that share a project must agree on them.  The integration project is built with -p:BuildIntegrationFixtures=false because its fixture target builds every fixture inside one MSBuild process (Uno.Sdk 6.6.42 then clashes with the already resolved 6.5.31, MSB4240); a lane that needs a fixture lists that fixture's own csproj as an entry 'project' so it builds in its own process.

A lane with 'needsNuGetCache' also downloads the build job's NuGet package cache: the IDE host resolves its LibreWPF assemblies from the global packages folder at run time, so a lane that starts the IDE (the integration lanes) needs it; the unit lane does not.

'buildLast' projects are built after everything else, with their own 'args' ('{rid}' is the platform's 'rid').  The host is built last with '--runtime <rid> -p:AppendRuntimeIdentifierToOutputPath=false', the recipe terminal-cross-platform.yml uses (it builds the Terminal add-in that way, which builds the host project it references as that RID into the same folder) and whose IDE does start on the Windows runner.  Measured on the runner without it: the host's OpenDevelop.deps.json is 166 libraries without a 'PresentationFramework/11.0.0.0' reference entry from the very first host build on, whatever is built afterwards in the default way (a macOS build has 193, with 28 'reference' entries for the LibreWPF assemblies), and the IDE dies at start-up with a FileNotFoundException for PresentationFramework 11.0.0.0.  The build summary records the host deps.json after every build, so the run shows what the RID-specific build changes.

A lane definition holds 'timeoutMinutes', optionally 'needsNuGetCache' (the IDE host resolves its LibreWPF assemblies from the global packages folder at run time), 'needsGtk' for native GTK dependencies, and 'entryTimeoutMinutes' (an entry's default budget).

'additionalProjects' declares fixture projects needed by an enabled entry; optional platforms refer to the build platform, so Windows ARM64 prerequisites belong to windows-x64 when it supplies the shared archive.

Profiler and Terminal are entries here; their own workflows (profiler.yml, terminal-cross-platform.yml) were deleted when they were folded in. Windows ARM64 and macOS ARM64 start as observed Terminal journeys and are promoted after repeated green runs.

platformNotes.macos-arm64: dist.macos.sh ships an osx-arm64-only payload, so this platform builds for itself and its archive drops the Windows RID trees the package never contains.
platformNotes.windows-x64: Every unit and integration entry is required here since 2026-10-27 (base-tests and xamldom-tests-microsoftwpf were the last unit entries promoted), so focus mode schedules no Windows x64 job beyond the build, which windows-arm64 still needs.
platformNotes.windows-arm64: Runs the native Windows ARM64 Terminal journey against the same unified Windows payload the x64 lane tests: dist.windows.bat ships one package with runtimes/ plus per-RID win-x64/win-arm64 folders and both launchers, so 'buildFrom': 'windows-x64' keeps a single compile for both lanes.
platformNotes.linux-x64: Enabled on 2026-11-02 with the unit suites (Profiler among them, which profiler.yml once ran on ubuntu-latest) and the workbench and DevFlow journeys, all 'observe'. The IDE entries run under xvfb-run with Mesa's software Vulkan driver (install-linux-prerequisites.sh); promote per the usual two green runs.
platformNotes.linux-arm64: Same entries and rules as linux-x64, on the native ubuntu-24.04-arm runner: dist.linux.sh ships one archive per Linux architecture, so each builds for itself.

unit.note: The unit suites, run like every other lane from the archive of their platform's build, in parallel with the integration lanes; Windows ARM64 ('buildFrom': 'windows-x64') runs the x64 build it ships. An entry gets 10 minutes, so one that hangs (for example a test whose child application cannot open a window) cannot use up the whole lane; the longest measured entry took about a minute (base-tests 61-64 s, profiler-tests 43-44 s on the Linux unit jobs of run 41393644443), and the lane's 45 minutes leave room for unpacking the archive and restoring the package cache.

integration-stable.note: Entries that passed on every hosted run in which the IDE started (runs 40431285339 through 40461019311): workbench, the stable core journeys, code coverage and the ARM64 unit suites, sharing one preparation. Windows x64 measured about 28 minutes of tests plus ~15 minutes of preparation. Its entries are required on macOS ARM64 and Windows x64 after each passed on the last two hosted runs that completed it there; on Windows ARM64 they are required too, after passing on runs 40444468212, 40461019311 and 40470967407. In focus mode the lane has no entry left and is not scheduled. new-project-dialog-macos joined later: it failed on the hosted runner until cc569fd5a8 and moved here after passing runs 40606824351 and 40615707034.

integration-unstable.note: Entries with known hosted failures or under investigation: macOS Terminal pointer input and debugger-journeys on Windows ARM64 (one flaky stop, fixed in c7497292df, awaiting a second green run). base-tests-arm, add-reference-journey and debugger-feature-journeys are required on every platform since 2026-10-28 but stay here for now: moving them into integration-stable would lengthen a lane with a 55-minute timeout that nobody has re-measured, and a full run is not due yet. Plan order runs Hot Reload last so a hang there does not hide the others.

integration-designer.note: All designer journeys (LibreWPF, LibreWinForms, MewUI, GTK) in one job. Entries in a lane run serially, so the LibreWPF journeys that edit src/Samples still never share the sample with a concurrent test. Windows: ~15 minutes preparation, 3.5 minutes GTK install, 24-28 minutes of LibreWPF editing.

buildLast.note: macOS and Linux are single-architecture payloads (dist.macos.sh, dist.linux.sh), so building the add-in for that RID is harmless and stages the native Terminal assets the lanes use. On Windows the unified payload already carries runtimes/win-x64 and win-arm64, so a RID build is what used to strip the host folder - the build guard rejects it there.
Publish the Windows host after the RID-specific Terminal build restores its mutable payload outputs.

entries.note: Microsoft's XamlReader is loaded on its own STA thread with a 20-second deadline; on a cold runner the first cases can exceed it and report HANG. One case failed that way on 2026-10-25 while the other 96 passed.

entries.note: First batch-4 cross-platform integration entry. Opens an isolated Razor SDK project and asserts HTML, CSS, JavaScript and C# highlighting through the running IDE. Measured locally on macOS ARM64: 1 test in 28 seconds; keep observe until repeated runner results are stable.

macOS ARM64: 7 passed and the Windows-only SDK download case skipped. On the hosted runner it failed until cc569fd5a8 (templates from the runtime-matching SDK folder only), then passed runs 40606824351 and 40615707034.
Covers template dialogs and project creation. The SDK-selection theory is excluded on Windows because one data row installs an SDK over the network; schedule it separately with its own time budget.

Exercises the modal Add Reference dialog with native clicks and verifies project and assembly references. It passes on hosted macOS ARM64 and Windows x64; on Windows ARM64 the dialog never got native focus because the image sits on the first-logon privacy page; the Prepare the Windows desktop step (32fd2eda79) clears it, and it then passed runs 40662664664 and 40671568295 there.
Protects integration fixture port ownership and cleanup on initialization failure.
Full profiler journeys, including capture isolation, web service, heap, launch and test-host profiling. macOS ARM64 locally passed 21 cases with the Windows WPF case skipped in 107 seconds.

30 LibreWPF designer editing journeys. Hosted Windows x64 (1389 s) and ARM64 (1569 s) passed all 30 in runs 40595645276 and 40606824351; hosted macOS ARM64 still fails CtrlPointerGestures_DistinguishClickCollapseFromGroupDrag.

Twelve GTK host, native preview, editing, recovery and libadwaita journeys passed locally on macOS ARM64 in 66 seconds. Hosted Windows x64 passed all twelve on runs 40495471973 and 40524161593; Windows ARM64 failed the toolbox drag onto the native surface until the desktop preparation step (32fd2eda79), then passed all twelve in runs 40662664664 and 40671568295. Exercises breakpoint inspection, stepping, restart and attaching to an independently started process. On the hosted macOS runner every attach hung in ICorDebug.DebugActiveProcess until ci.yml granted system.privilege.taskport (a24f882e56); with it, both debugger entries passed runs 40582707365 and 40595645276. On Windows ARM64 one case failed until e2dc739e95 mapped the x64 build job's source paths onto the ARM64 workspace; it then passed runs 40662664664 and 40671568295.

Exercises real WPF application and class-library Hot Reload journeys; Microsoft WPF variants run only on Windows. macOS ARM64 locally passed four journeys with two Windows-only skips.
